key_insight: Greedy decoding is not fully deterministic across numeric precisions: BF16 and FP16 can produce different LLM outputs on the same prompt and hardware.
engineering_relevance: Precision choice can materially affect inference reproducibility, so systems that require stable outputs may need selective higher-precision safeguards rather than assuming greedy decoding is deterministic.
method: Compared BF16 vs FP16 greedy decoding across six models and three benchmarks.
Analyzed error propagation, focusing on LM-head top-two logit margins versus directional perturbations.
Tested selective FP32 LM-head recomputation as a low-overhead mitigation.
evidence_signal: Across six models (1.1B-7B, with 12B characterized) and three benchmarks, 49-100% of prompts diverged, and the selective FP32 LM-head intervention improved exact agreement by 22-36 percentage points on A10G with under 4% latency overhead in low-batch inference.
watch_item: The mitigation is not universal: it loses effectiveness when body-originated error dominates, especially at batch size >=8 and under end-to-end FP8.
paper_title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
